macro.regime: Cautious, event-dense grind: sanctions largely defused, AI-capex test and Jackson Hole still ahead
macro.narrative: Levels below are the complete Monday 24 Aug US close: S&P 500 7,652.86 (-0.28%), Nasdaq 25,980.19 (-0.77%), Dow 53,417.16 (+0.26%), VIX 15.85 (+4.76%, still near 2026's compressed lows) -- a narrow, mildly risk-off session concentrated in mega-cap chip names (Micron -5.8%, AMD -3.3%, TSM -3.7%, Nvidia -2.3%) ahead of Wednesday's earnings, while Dow/Materials/Staples/Financials held up. The week's first binary catalyst has now resolved with less drama than feared: Bessent's Monday 2pm ET rollout ('Operation Economic Outcast', corrected from 'Economic Fury') designated ~60 entities and five new secondary-sanctions categories phased in over time rather than immediate blanket measures, and pointedly did not name China directly despite pointed rhetoric -- oil actually sold off 2.5% on 'sell the news' profit-taking after two weeks of anticipatory rally, and Iran's Hormuz threat remains unexecuted. Separately, US-Canada trade talks collapsed and the US imposed 50% tariffs on ~$20bn of Canadian goods -- a second, lower-profile trade-friction front. Gold extended to a 3-month high on the same Treasury-buyback dollar-weakness trade (DXY near a 3-month low) that is also lifting Bitcoin toward $80k; in Asia, Korea's KOSPI fell 3.1% Monday on the same pre-Nvidia chip jitters (foreign/institutional selling absorbed almost entirely by retail buying), with a similar pullback in Hong Kong tech names even as Southbound Stock Connect flow flipped back to a net buy. Two binary catalysts remain this week: Nvidia's FQ2 print (Wed 26 Aug after close) and new Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri 28 Aug). Net: a modest uptick in risk-on conviction now that the sanctions overhang resolved without a shock, offset by the still-live Nvidia/Jackson Hole event risk and the fresh Canada-tariff friction.

drivers.factor: Iran sanctions rollout landed Monday with less immediate bite than feared -- 'Operation Economic Outcast', ~60 entities, phased secondary sanctions
drivers.read: Bessent's 2pm ET announcement designated roughly 60 entities/vessels/individuals (UAE, HK, China, Singapore, Switzerland) and unveiled five new secondary-sanctions categories (digital assets, tech, gold, aviation, shipping) to be phased in via country-by-country deadlines, not imposed immediately. Asked about Chinese banks, Bessent said 'no one is above the reach of U.S. sanctions' without naming China directly -- oil sold off 2.5% on the news (sell-the-rumor-buy... sell-the-fact) after two weeks of anticipatory rally. Iran's Hormuz threat remains rhetorical, unexecuted as of this run.

drivers.factor: US-Canada trade war escalates -- a second, lower-profile tariff front
drivers.read: Talks collapsed Friday 21 Aug; the US imposed 50% tariffs on ~$20bn of Canadian goods (building materials, liquor, some apparel), Canada vowed to match dollar-for-dollar. No direct read-through to the tracked universe's core names, but adds to the week's cumulative trade-friction backdrop alongside the still-unresolved China secondary-sanctions question.

drivers.factor: Nvidia FQ2 earnings (Wed 26 Aug after close) is now one trading day away, after Monday's pre-earnings chip selloff
drivers.read: Micron, AMD, TSM and Nvidia itself all fell Monday (-1.3% to -5.8%) as AI-capex-fatigue positioning built into the print -- the cleanest single test of whether the mid-August capex-durability scare (WSJ's ~$3tn off-balance-sheet AI-commitments estimate) is real or overdone.

drivers.factor: Jackson Hole (27-29 Aug) remains the week's other binary catalyst -- Warsh's untested debut keynote Friday
drivers.read: Unchanged from the prior run: Warsh has previewed his remarks as 'long-term structural questions, not near-term guidance'; a BofA survey shows 69% expecting a neutral tone, futures price roughly 1-in-3 odds of a September hike.

drivers.factor: Debasement trade (gold, Bitcoin) extends on the Treasury-buyback dollar slide
drivers.read: Gold hit a 3-month high Monday (spot ~$4,649-4,681, GLD +0.79% to $426.69) and Bitcoin traded $78,000-79,140 (+22% on the week, nearing $80k) on the same dollar-weakness mechanism (DXY near a 3-month low ~98.8) -- both a debasement hedge and a liquidity-driven risk asset moving together, not a pure fear rotation.

drivers.factor: Korea/HK tech pullback Monday tracks the same pre-Nvidia chip jitters, not a distinct regional shock
drivers.read: KOSPI fell 3.1% Monday (foreign/institutional selling of ~W5-5.5trn combined almost entirely absorbed by retail buying) as Samsung/SK Hynix dropped; Hong Kong Southbound flipped from a Friday outflow to a Monday inflow but sold SMIC specifically even as it bought Tencent/Alibaba -- a stock-specific divergence rather than a broad China/HK de-risking.

byAssetClass.note: Held Neutral: Monday's mixed close (Dow up, S&P/Nasdaq down on chip weakness) with the sanctions catalyst now resolved without a shock argues for a marginal upgrade, but Nvidia earnings (Wed) and Jackson Hole (Fri) are both still live -- staying Neutral rather than re-risking into two more binary events this week.

Held OW: gold extended to a 3-month high Monday on the same Treasury-buyback dollar-weakness trade even as oil sold off on sanctions 'sell the news' -- the metals leg of the hard-asset rotation remains intact and is now the stronger half of the commodity complex.

Held modest OW: BTC continues grinding higher on Treasury-buyback-driven liquidity optimism, but gave back roughly a third of Friday's surge over the weekend (~$76,000 Sunday vs $78,335 Friday close) on thin weekend liquidity -- a level, not a close, and not treated as a reversal.

Held Neutral: the FOMC minutes' hawkish bloc (3 dissents for a hike) is offset by dovish Sept-cut pricing (~65% for 25bp), but historically tight credit spreads (HY OAS ~271-281bp, richest decile) leave the credit sleeve (HYG/LQD) more exposed than the rate sleeve if Jackson Hole surprises hawkish or September issuance tests demand.

Held Neutral: the sanctions rollout resolved without naming China directly, reducing the acute dollar-defensive setup flagged last run, but DXY still sits near a 3-month low on the Treasury-buyback mechanism -- cash optionality into Nvidia/Jackson Hole remains reasonable even as the acute trigger passed.
